stem.text: Oil leaks out of a storage drum at a rate of R(t) gallons per hour, where R is a positive function and t is measured in hours. Using correct units, interpret the meaning of \( \frac{1}{6}\int_{10}^{16} R(t)\,dt \) in the context of the problem.

answer_key.label: It is the average rate at which oil leaks out of the drum over the time interval from \( t = 10 \) to \( t = 16 \) hours, measured in gallons per hour.

worked_solution.text: R(t) is a rate measured in gallons per hour, so integrating it over time multiplies by hours and gives an amount in gallons.
worked_solution.rule_named: units of a definite integral of a rate

worked_solution.text: The limits run from \( t = 10 \) to \( t = 16 \) hours, so \( \int_{10}^{16} R(t)\,dt \) is the total amount of oil that leaks out of the drum from \( t = 10 \) to \( t = 16 \) hours.
worked_solution.rule_named: integral of a rate is the accumulated change

worked_solution.text: Dividing by the length of the interval, 6 hours, turns the amount into an average rate, so the expression is the average rate at which oil leaks out of the drum from \( t = 10 \) to \( t = 16 \) hours, in gallons per hour.

options.label: It is the average rate at which oil leaks out of the drum over the whole time the model covers, measured in gallons per hour.
